summary: A GMDSS ship's satellite gear: Inmarsat-C, GPS, LRIT and Fleet Broadband, how each works, and how to reason out common faults.

blocks.title: Ship to shore
items: Terminal, uplink, satellite, downlink, LES (Land Earth Station), shore networks.
Inmarsat satellites are geostationary: each covers an ocean region.

blocks.title: Weak signals
items: LNA, low noise amplifier: receives and amplifies the very weak satellite signal, at or near the antenna. It sets the noise figure.
SNR, signal to noise ratio: compares signal level to background noise level. 10 dB: signal power is 10 × noise power.
Fade margin: a design allowance for expected fading.

blocks.title: Inmarsat-C: text only
items: Store-and-forward: the LES stores each message, then forwards it. No voice, so no VoIP.
NCS, Network Coordination Station: just 1 per ocean region per system.
EGC, Enhanced Group Call: SafetyNET, FleetNET and System messages.
LOOP BACK test: send yourself a test message.
Ground the terminal chassis, to minimize shock hazard, and the antenna, to its mast.
Antenna: RHC (right-hand circular), omni-directional, mounted high, free from shadowing.

blocks.title: GPS
items: Usual arrangement: 24 satellites, 6 orbital planes, 4 per plane, 20,200 km altitude, 55° inclination.
At least 4 satellites for highest accuracy.
DGPS, Differential GPS: a fixed station transmits corrections by radio.
Bridge link: NMEA-0183 or NMEA-2000 LAN.

blocks.title: LRIT
items: LRIT, Long Range Identification and Tracking: a GPS position sent over Inmarsat-C. A separate tracking system for each flag state's security.
APR, automatic position report: every 6 hours, at least 4 a day. A poll gets a PR, position report, back automatically.
Not reporting? Check the GMDSS console's Inmarsat-C terminal.

blocks.title: Fleet Broadband
items: Calls and Internet: maritime BGAN, Broadband Global Area Network.
Radome: stabilized antenna, RF unit, Antenna Control Unit, GPS antenna.
SIM: integrated circuit device storing the Inmarsat identity and an authentication key. PUK, PIN Unlock Key, unlocks it.
Streaming: exclusive, high priority, time critical. Standard IP is shared: a busy channel lowers the bit rate.
Distress test: arranged with the LES in advance, via service number 33.

blocks.title: Faults
head: Symptom
Answer
rows: Short coax end: above 1 ohm, replace
EL step motor, power off: stiff, replace
In ISDN port, or wrong IP address
3-30 MHz or radars; ferrite clamps for HF

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: GPS doesn't support LRIT: it only broadcasts.
LRIT isn't AIS or AMVER.
Never insulate the antenna from its mast.
IP handset: no polling, and it doesn't power the terminal.
Fax: no Group 5, no 5.1 kHz.
